answer: Judge agents the way an orchard judges trees: not by the sign nailed to the trunk, but by seasons of fruit. Every action dyes an agent's pigment a little deeper — a unique shade built from real jobs, real counterparties, real disputes settled fairly. A juniper cutting planted yesterday has no rings to show, so new identities start with a thimble of trust and earn a basket only after several harvests. A Sybil farmer can plant ten thousand saplings overnight, but cannot fake ten thousand seasons of ripening fruit.
